queries: LLM performance degrades with longer context study 2025
METR measuring AI ability to complete long software tasks
SWE-bench LLM agents maintain production software

sources_considered.why: Controlled study showing LLM performance drops as input length grows. Bears on the 'break down' sub-claim.
Independent measurement of how long a software task AI agents can reliably complete. Context on both sides.

receipt.public_excerpt: We demonstrate that even under these minimal conditions, model performance degrades as input length increases, often in surprising and non-uniform ways.

evidence_items.explanation: Consistent with the sub-claim that LLMs break down as they are given more input. The tasks are simple retrieval and replication, not code, so this cannot settle the software engineering claim.

evidence_items.locator: Summary section, paragraph on current models

receipt.public_excerpt: the best current models—such as Claude 3.7 Sonnet—are capable of some tasks that take even expert humans hours, but can only reliably complete tasks of up to a few minutes long.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows models could reliably complete only short software tasks as of early 2025, while also reporting that this capability was growing fast. Neither finding tests the speaker's definition of software engineering.

unresolved_gaps: No agreed benchmark measures 'software engineering' in the speaker's sense: long-term understanding and maintenance of functional software.
What 'learn' and 'adapt' mean is not settled by his words.
